root_idea.summary: The root centers on falling or coming down, with extensions to something occurring or befalling, a place where something settles, and the causing or marking of an event.
root_idea.development: From the basic notion of falling, the lexical network develops meanings of occurrence, descent and settlement, battlefield impact, physical marking, and derived causation or expectation. These root-level developments do not apply as direct meanings to every Quranic form.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form I citation وَقَعَ.
The inflected Quran form is normalized to the Form IV citation أَوْقَعَ.
The Quranic plural is normalized to the supported singular noun مَوْقِع.
The attached-pronoun masculine plural is normalized to the active-participle citation form مُوَاقِع.
Displayed as the active participle/adjective وَاقِع.
Displayed as the substantivized feminine active participle وَاقِعَة.
The inflected Quran noun is normalized to the citation form وَقْعَة.

senses.definition: To fall or descend; to come down upon a place or into a position.
senses.usage_conditions: Includes the Quranic construction فَقَعُوا لَهُ سَاجِدِينَ, expressing prompt falling into prostration.

senses.definition: To occur, happen, or befall; to come to pass.
senses.usage_conditions: Used of an event, state, affliction, or other matter that comes about or falls upon someone.

senses.definition: To take effect so that an expressed matter becomes binding, realized, or fulfilled.
senses.usage_conditions: In Quranic expressions concerning a statement, promised punishment, or reward, وقوع denotes the realization of its substantive implication, including its becoming due or incumbent.

senses.definition: To cause something to occur or befall; to bring about a result.
senses.usage_conditions: A causative transitive use; in the Quranic occurrence, the object is enmity and hatred, which are caused to arise between people.

senses.definition: A place or position where something falls, settles, or is set.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic plural مَوَاقِع refers to the positions or settings of the stars.

senses.definition: Falling into or encountering something; one who is to fall into it.
senses.usage_conditions: Active participle of وَاقَعَ, used with an object; the Quranic form has an attached pronoun referring to the object entered or encountered.

senses.definition: Occurring, befalling, or certain to occur.
senses.usage_conditions: An active participle functioning adjectivally or substantively; Quranic contexts frequently present the event as sure to happen.

senses.definition: The momentous event or severe occurrence; in the Quran, the decisive eschatological Event.
senses.usage_conditions: A feminine active participle used as a substantive; الوَاقِعَةُ is associated with a severe or unwelcome event and in the cited Quranic passages denotes the final judgmental event.

senses.definition: The occurrence or coming to pass of an event.
senses.usage_conditions: In لِوَقْعَتِهَا, the noun refers specifically to the occurrence of the momentous Event.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To fall into or come to be in a place, situation, or trap; to light upon or reach something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with constructions such as فِي and إِلَى; the range includes entering a difficulty or period of scarcity, finding oneself in a desert or meadow, becoming ensnared, and drifting to a destination.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To fall, lie, or close upon or against something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of an object or part of an object lying against a surface or body, including a garment lying upon a particular part.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To originate an event and make it befall.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative construction of Form I, distinct from the ordinary intransitive use of وَقَعَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To fall upon people in battle; to make an onslaught or inflict heavy slaughter.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A military construction denoting a forceful attack or vehement engagement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To slander, revile, defame, or detract from a person's reputation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A speech-related construction involving hostile or damaging remarks about someone in their absence or otherwise.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To serve a need, stand in stead, or have an effect.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of something that sufficiently meets a need or produces a discernible effect; the expression may describe how a matter stands with someone.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a word or expression, to apply to a thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A construction concerning the referent or applicability of an expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An occasion or circumstance in which one falls into sin.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Literally a place of falling; used figuratively for a situation that leads to sinful involvement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To sign, endorse, or append an authoritative note or concise annotation to a writing; also, the appended note itself.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The entry describes a later administrative and scribal usage, including signing or adding a postil to a completed document.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To blame or reprove someone angrily or severely.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive reproach construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To approach or come near to doing or experiencing affairs or events.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of being close to undertaking or undergoing something; the source equates it with approaching it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To experience an occurrence or meet with something that happens.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive construction focused on undergoing or encountering an event.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To have sexual intercourse with someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional euphemistic use of the Form III verbal noun مُوَاقَعَة and its verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To engage with people in fighting or conflict.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A military use denoting participation in combat.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause someone to fall into a trap or the like; to ensnare him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative construction with a person as the affected object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To punish someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive construction in which the person is subjected to punishment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To put something into a person's heart or mind.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative mental-placement construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To incite discord or strife between people.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with people or groups as the parties between whom trouble is caused.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To expect something and look for its coming to pass.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expectation is oriented toward the anticipated occurrence or arrival of the thing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An onslaught or shock in battle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: May refer to a single assault or to an engagement of the same kind when repeated.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A wisp of wool or similar material used to tar a mangy camel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized technical use concerning treatment of a camel's mange.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person who habitually makes others fall into evil or mischief.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intensive personal description, reported as an approximate lexical explanation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An event, fact, or case; reality in the expression فِي الوَاقِعِ.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A substantivized or idiomatic Classical use distinct from the Quranic predicative sense “occurring” or “certain to occur.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: A cadence in music.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized musical meaning of the verbal noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Efficient or effective.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival description of something producing a result.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Tried or experienced.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive-participial adjective describing someone or something tested by experience.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Occurrence or coming to pass is represented under Form I.
Coming upon or becoming in a place.
Falling into a period of scarcity is covered by the broader fall-into construction.
Coming or drifting to a destination.
Falling or lying upon or against something.
Becoming ensnared is covered by falling into a trap or situation.
Coming to be in a desert or meadow.
A garment lying against a body part.
Falling upon an enemy in attack.
Supplying or sufficing for a need.
Standing with someone in good or bad stead.
Applicability of a word to a thing.
Plunging or falling into an affair or activity.
Explicit Quran-attested construction of falling into a thing.
Causation of an event or result.
Causing someone to fall into a trap.
Causing evil to befall people is covered by the Quranic causative sense.
Putting something into the heart or mind.
A person who causes others to fall into evil.
Reality in the idiom فِي الوَاقِعِ.
An occasion or place of falling into sin.
The expression's possible sense of having an effect.
An effect produced by an item given as charity.

cautions: A Lane Quran citation attached to the وَاقَعَ construction uses a historical citation convention and is not treated as a modern verse location; the example location shown here comes from the independently supplied QAC occurrence.
The Form I senses distinguish simple falling or occurrence from the Quranic construction in which a statement, promise, or reward becomes effective or binding.
